 Matthew Rhys reveals embarrassing moment that ruined his chances of becoming 007
 Matthew Rhys has opened up about an awkward moment when he missed out on James Bond role following a casting meeting
 By 
 Web Desk 
 | 
 Published November 20, 2026 
 Despite missing out on Bond, Matthew subsequently established himself as a leading television actor Matthew Rhys has opened up about an awkward moment when he missed out on James Bond role following a casting meeting.
 The Cardiff-born actor, 52, recalled the unforgettable incident in which he lost out on one of cinema's most coveted roles during an appearance on Conan O'Brien's podcast.
 The audition took place at the Bond producers' offices overlooking Green Park in London.
 READ MORE:  Matthew Rhys explains 'fun' in playing 'mildly sadistic' Nile in 'The Beast in Me' 
 When asked by Conan O'Brien, 63, how the meeting had gone, Matthew replied: 'Well I'm not playing Bond, nor have I been.'
 During the interview, the conversation took an unexpected turn when the audition panel asked him to explain how he would approach the character differently.
 The panel asked: 'So what would you do different with Bond?'
 Matthew said: 'As a terrible joke, I said, 'Limp'.
 Rather than changing course, the actor continued with the joke, suggesting his version of Bond should also wear an eye patch.
 He recalled: 'It went very quiet and then I just fell apart.'
 The meeting failed to secure Matthew the role, which eventually went to Daniel, whose interpretation of the British spy began with Casino Royale and continued through four further films.
 Daniel went on to star in Quantum of Solace, Skyfall, Spectre and No Time to Die , ending his 15-year tenure as 007 in 2021.
 Despite missing out on Bond, Matthew subsequently established himself as a leading television actor, becoming particularly well known for playing Soviet intelligence officer Philip Jennings in the acclaimed spy drama The Americans.
